promptText: Which select-service hotel brands are commonly considered for new-build projects in the Caribbean and Latin America?

payload.rawResponseText:
For **new-build select-service hotels in the Caribbean and Latin America**, the following brands are commonly included in initial feasibility and flag-selection exercises. Availability varies significantly by country, territory and protected franchise area.

### Core brands frequently screened

| Brand family | Common candidates | Typical positioning/use |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott** | **Courtyard**, **Fairfield by Marriott**, **City Express by Marriott**, **Four Points by Sheraton** | Courtyard and Four Points for upscale commercial, airport and mixed-use locations; Fairfield and City Express for more cost-conscious upper-midscale or midscale projects. |
|  | **AC Hotels**, **Aloft**, **Moxy** | Lifestyle-oriented select service for urban centers, entertainment districts and higher-ADR leisure markets. |
| **Hilton** | **Hampton by Hilton**, **Hilton Garden Inn**, **Tru by Hilton**, **Spark by Hilton** | Hampton and HGI are established regional candidates; Tru and Spark are increasingly considered for efficient new builds and more price-sensitive markets. |
| **Hyatt** | **Hyatt Place** | One of Hyatt’s principal select-service options in the region, particularly for airports, business districts and mixed-use projects. |
| **IHG** | **Holiday Inn Express** | A standard contender for upper-midscale commercial, highway and airport demand. |
|  | **avid hotels**, **Garner** | Newer or emerging regional alternatives; market and country availability must be confirmed. |
| **Accor** | **ibis**, **ibis Styles**, **ibis budget** | Particularly important in Brazil and parts of South America; generally suited to efficient economy and midscale development. |
|  | **Novotel**, sometimes **Mercure** | Leaner midscale/upscale projects, although individual hotels may operate closer to full service. |
| **Wyndham** | **La Quinta by Wyndham**, **Wyndham Garden**, **Microtel by Wyndham** | Common midscale-to-upper-midscale alternatives, especially where development cost and operational efficiency are priorities. |
| **Choice Hotels** | **Comfort**, **Sleep Inn**, sometimes **Quality Inn** or **Country Inn & Suites by Radisson** | Most relevant in Mexico and selected CALA markets; usually positioned in midscale or upper-midscale segments. |

Marriott formally groups Courtyard, Fairfield, City Express, Four Points, AC, Aloft and Moxy within its broader select-service portfolio, and City Express is specifically marketed for development across Mexico, Latin America and the Caribbean. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/select-brands?utm_source=openai))

Hilton currently reports more than 90 focused-service hotels in its CALA pipeline, led by Hampton, Hilton Garden Inn, Tru and Spark; Home2 Suites is also entering the region. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hilton-ends-2025-with-robust-luxury-and-lifestyle-growth-across-the-caribbean-and-latin-america?utm_source=openai)) Hyatt’s principal proven regional options remain Hyatt Place and, for longer stays, Hyatt House. ([newsroom.hyatt.com](https://newsroom.hyatt.com/2024-10-03-Hyatt-Select-Service-Pipeline-in-the-Americas-Grows-by-More-than-25-Over-the-Past-Three-Years-Including-Over-4%2C000-Pipeline-Hyatt-Studios-Rooms?utm_source=openai)) IHG identifies Holiday Inn Express, Garner and avid within its Essentials portfolio in Mexico, Latin America and the Caribbean. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2026/key-openings-brand-debuts-fuel-growth-across-mlac-region-for-ihg-hotels-and-resorts?utm_source=openai))

### Extended-stay alternatives

Where the demand study identifies stays of five nights or longer—industrial projects, medical demand, relocation, energy, infrastructure or airline crews—the shortlist may also include:

- **Home2 Suites by Hilton**
- **Hyatt House**
- **Residence Inn by Marriott**
- **TownePlace Suites by Marriott**
- **Element by Marriott**
- **Staybridge Suites**
- **Candlewood Suites**
- **Hawthorn Extended Stay by Wyndham**

Home2 Suites is still an emerging CALA product rather than an established regional default, while Marriott officially classifies Residence Inn, TownePlace Suites and Element alongside its select-service and extended-stay offerings. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hilton-ends-2025-with-robust-luxury-and-lifestyle-growth-across-the-caribbean-and-latin-america?utm_source=openai))

### Regional and country-specific brands

- **Mexico:** **one hoteles** and **Fiesta Inn/Fiesta Inn Express** from Posadas should generally be included in the competitive review. One is Posadas’ economy product, while Fiesta Inn targets business-oriented demand; both have appeared in the company’s development pipeline. ([posadas.com](https://www.posadas.com/web/posadas/hoteles?utm_source=openai))
- **Brazil and Southern Cone:** Accor’s **ibis family** is often one of the most relevant benchmarks, with Novotel and Mercure considered at higher rate points. Accor identifies ibis, Novotel and Mercure as central to its economy and midscale development strategy. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/midscale-economy-brands-novotel-mercure-ibis?utm_source=openai))
- **Selected Mexico/CALA markets:** Choice’s **Comfort** and **Sleep Inn** have supported both new construction and conversions in the region. ([media.choicehotels.com](https://media.choicehotels.com/2024-20-04-Choice-Hotels-CALA-abre-dos-hoteles-en-Puebla-Comfort-Sleep?utm_source=openai))

### Practical “first-call” shortlist

For a conventional **100–180-key urban, airport or commercial new build**, I would normally begin with:

1. Courtyard  
2. Fairfield  
3. City Express  
4. Hampton  
5. Hilton Garden Inn  
6. Tru  
7. Hyatt Place  
8. Holiday Inn Express  
9. ibis or ibis Styles  
10. La Quinta  
11. Wyndham Garden  
12. Comfort or Sleep Inn  

Then add **AC, Aloft or Moxy** for a higher-ADR lifestyle location, and **Home2 Suites, Hyatt House or Residence Inn** if extended-stay demand is material.

The final shortlist should be narrowed based on **country-specific brand availability, projected ADR, room count, required food-and-beverage program, loyalty-program contribution, franchise and reservation fees, staffing model, local construction costs, hurricane/seismic codes and territorial protection**. A flag that works in Mexico City or São Paulo may not have an economically viable prototype for a smaller Caribbean island.
